key_bets: KrF excimer ASPEN laser architecture with NLO pulse compression achieves $60-80/J at NOAK, requiring 25x reduction in capacitor cost to <$0.40/J via in-house manufacturing
Capsule gain Qc > 200 at 8-12 MJ on target, extrapolated from NIF's ~34 at 250 kJ via 2/3 power-law scaling (never validated above NIF scale)
Two-beam Hybrid Direct Drive (HDD) implosion achieves symmetric ignition using ring-shaped intensity profile and hohlraum pre-pulse, with only two beam penetrations through the chamber
FLiBe thick-liquid-wall chamber clears vaporized coolant (<10 kg/shot) via gravity within ~1 second, sustaining 0.25-1 Hz rep rate
Laser wall-plug efficiency of 5-7% maintained at MJ scale (demonstrated only at 750 J on NRL Electra)
SBS/NLO pulse compression preserves beam wavefront quality at >100 kJ per pulse to maintain implosion symmetry
FLiNaK substitution for FLiBe in commercial plants maintains adequate TBR (~1.05) via (n,2n) reactions, eliminating beryllium supply chain
eliminated_costs: Superconducting magnet system (C220103 = $0) — no TF/PF coils required in IFE
First-wall and divertor replacement cycle — thick FLiBe liquid wall self-renews each shot
Auxiliary plasma heating and current-drive systems (NBI, ECRH, ICRH) — pulsed IFE has no plasma to sustain
Final focusing optics refurbishment (>$40M/year at NIF) — Xcimer geometry keeps optics outside neutron/X-ray flux zone
Lithium-6 enrichment — thick liquid wall with large capsule yield breeds adequately from natural lithium
novel_costs: Laser driver capital ($600-800M NOAK at 10 MJ, $1,500-2,000/kWe) — dominates plant capex with no vendor ecosystem or independent cost history at MJ scale
Per-shot DT target consumables at 8-31 million targets/year (0.25-1 Hz) — recurring cost with no MFE analogue, $2-3/target Goodin ceiling
In-house capacitor manufacturing facility (Tucson, AZ) — vertical-integration capex committed before plant validation
FLiBe thick-liquid-wall chamber with precision jet formation, pumps, nozzles, and redox chemistry control — no industrial precedent at fusion conditions
Target fabrication and injection infrastructure for sub-Hz high-reliability shot cadence (plastic ablator + liquid DT precision sphericity at mass throughput)

risks.description: Laser $/J NOAK target ($60-80/J) is self-reported, unverified, and depends on untested MJ-scale NLO architecture plus 25x capacitor cost reduction
Capsule gain extrapolation from NIF (Qc ~34 at 250 kJ) to Xcimer (Qc >200 at 10 MJ) via 2/3 power-law is unvalidated; Betti 2024 calls even ~100x gain 'unclear' at few-MJ scale

Two-beam HDD implosion symmetry has no experimental demonstration; Anvil (2028) is first test, and failure is an architectural kill with no LCOE mitigation path because thick-liquid-wall requires exactly two beam penetrations
FLiBe chamber clearing dynamics at sub-Hz rep rate validated only by simulation and water/oil analogs; if clearing exceeds 1 second, rep rate drops below 0.25 Hz and LCOE rises 2-2.5x
SBS/NLO pulse compression phase-preservation at >100 kJ per pulse is unproven; degraded beam quality would compound two-beam symmetry challenge
Energy conversion cycle type unresolved (steam Rankine ~33% vs. He Brayton ~45%) — materially different gross thermal power requirements and BOP capital cost
Target fabrication cost per shot is proprietary and unvalidated at 8-31M/yr throughput; exceeding $2-3/target Goodin ceiling adds $11-22/MWh to LCOE (base excludes target cost entirely)
Plant availability/capacity factor has no maintenance model or component lifetime data; FLiBe pump/nozzle maintenance interval unknown
FLiBe → FLiNaK blanket transition between Athena and commercial plants is an architectural material change, not a learning-curve multiplier; cost delta is a blocking gap
NRL has moved primary US government gas-laser IFE program from KrF to ArF, leaving Xcimer's KrF MJ-scale scaling path without active government co-development at the same medium
Betti 2024 independent assessment: direct-drive implosion quality unlikely to rival indirect drive with current laser tech; Xcimer's two-beam geometry is a harder version of this problem
Tritium inventory claim of <200 g at GWe depends on rapid FLiBe extraction that has only been demonstrated at lab scale
Beryllium supply chain (Athena FLiBe) constrained by single US producer (Materion) at ~300 tonnes/yr global output with no industrial-scale FLiBe production
